---
title: Heteroskedasticity functions
---

## Recommended: one SymPy expression

Define a function in terms of `e` (the residual) and `z` (the optional shape
parameter). Paneltime derives the Python derivatives and generates the
ExprTk-compatible C++ expression.

```{python}
#| eval: false
import sympy as sp

e, z = sp.symbols("e z")
h_function = sp.log(e**2 + 1e-8)
results = model.fit(h_function=h_function)
```

At fit time, the Python and ExprTk implementations are evaluated on sample
values and checked for agreement. Unsupported SymPy constructs produce a
clear conversion error; use the manual dual implementation below as the
escape hatch.

SymPy is an optional dependency and must be installed to use symbolic
expressions. Use smooth, real-valued expressions whose first and second
derivatives exist on the residual domain. For example, use
`sp.sqrt(e**2 + 1e-8)` rather than `sp.Abs(e)`: the latter has a distributional
second derivative and is rejected with a conversion error.

If the expression contains `z`, paneltime adds an estimated shape parameter
named `z in h(e,z)`. This requires at least one ARCH lag; otherwise the shape
parameter cannot enter the variance recursion. It can be fixed using
`constraints={"z": 0.2}`. Avoid redundant specifications: for example,
`sp.exp(z)*e**2` confounds the shape parameter with the ARCH coefficients.
Successful compilation does not guarantee identification or convergence.

The expression defines the lagged variance innovation, not the likelihood
distribution or the variance link. Select `vol="EGARCH"` separately if a
log-variance model is intended. A custom expression must remain valid over
the residual and shape values encountered during estimation.

## Advanced: hand-writing the C++ expression directly

Custom likelihoods may still provide `h_val_cpp` and its Python counterpart.
The expression is parsed by ExprTk. Use `e`, `z`, and temporary variables
`x0` through `x4`. Python `**` becomes ExprTk `^`.

Multiple statements use `;`; the final expression is returned. ExprTk uses
`:=` for assignment. Logical `and`/`or` are unsupported, so arithmetic masks
must express conditions.

| Function | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `abs(x)` | Absolute value |
| `sqrt(x)` | Square root |
| `log(x)` | Natural logarithm |
| `exp(x)` | Exponential |
| `sin(x)`, `cos(x)`, `tan(x)` | Trigonometric functions |
| `floor(x)`, `ceil(x)` | Rounding |
| `min(x, y)`, `max(x, y)` | Bounds |
| `sign(x)` | Sign of a value |

```python
x0 := (e + z)^2; (x0 <= 1) * x0^2 + (x0 > 1) * x0
```

See the [ExprTk documentation](https://www.partow.net/programming/exprtk/)
for parser details.
